tasks.short: Determine the nature and extent of vehicle damage.

steps.what: Read actual work orders and relevant vehicle repair history
inputs: actual vehicle identifier and repair history
outputs: checked reported vehicle problem and history

steps.what: Confer with customers about actual symptoms and circumstances
inputs: checked reported vehicle problem and history
outputs: actual symptom details and customer constraints

steps.what: Examine vehicles to determine actual nature and extent of damage
inputs: actual symptom details and customer constraints
outputs: actual examined damage and diagnostic findings

steps.what: Enter and check actual damage findings in the existing work order
inputs: actual examined damage and diagnostic findings
actual work order and vehicle reference

steps.what: Save the checked final damage work-order entry

tasks.design: Configure native vehicle-history lookup and existing work-order defaults in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The technician discusses symptoms, examines the actual vehicle and records only verified findings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Diagnosis preparation and findings entry can repeat vehicle and work-order references.
tasks.enabler_now: Native vehicle links and structured finding fields can reduce repeated lookup and entry.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden damage, interacting systems and safe diagnosis require physical examination and technical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The technician reconciles customer symptoms with actual vehicle condition.
tasks.altitude: Less diagnostic administration; damage assessment stays human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: vehicle-linked service work orders can reuse history and reference fields; they do not diagnose vehicle damage.

assumptions: Actual intake owner supplies vehicle identifier, reported issue and existing work order. Technician verifies history in s1, obtains actual symptom details in s2 and creates actual examination findings in s3; unsupported fields stay manual in s4.
Conferencing, reading and examination can be alternative diagnostic paths. Shares are a provisional task mix, not a mandatory sequence per repair or a measured baseline; reweight actual paths.
Only an existing findings record is included. Native lookup and defaults first; already configured work earns no saving. Cuts cover repeated references, not capture of actual findings.
Routine save retains one percent and uses the existing final record check; no additional self-approval time is added.
unknowns: Which references are still entered twice?
How often is history lookup needed?
research_questions: Can native work-order context reduce administration without shortening examination?

incremental.description: Maintain vehicle/work-order links and finding-field defaults.

approvals.approved_version: s4 checked final actual damage entry and exact vehicle work-order destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 15*0.40 lookup + 14*0.20 reference entry = 8.8; minus 0.8 upkeep = 8. Half eligible gives 4.4 minus 0.8 = 3.6. Examination, conversation and save stay retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: List parts, estimate repair costs and plan work procedures.

steps.what: Retrieve actual parts lists, technical manuals and diagrams for the vehicle configuration
outputs: checked relevant parts and technical sources

steps.what: List parts needed and verify quantities and compatibility
inputs: checked relevant parts and technical sources
outputs: checked actual repair parts list and prices

steps.what: Calculate estimated parts and labour costs using actual selected quantities and rates
inputs: checked actual repair parts list and prices
actual approved labour rates and applicable charge rules

steps.what: Plan work procedures and actual labour requirements for the repair
inputs: checked relevant parts and technical sources
outputs: actual chosen work procedures and labour requirements

steps.what: Check the final parts list, estimate and planned procedures against actual repair requirements
inputs: actual chosen work procedures and labour requirements
checked actual repair parts list and prices
outputs: checked final repair estimate and work plan

steps.what: Save the checked final repair estimate and work plan
inputs: checked final repair estimate and work plan
outputs: saved actual repair estimate and plan

tasks.design: Configure native parts lookup, catalogue field reuse and estimate calculations in {OPS_SYSTEM}, using actual supplier information from {PROCUREMENT} and technical sources in {DOCS}. The technician chooses compatible parts and procedures, sets actual labour requirements and checks the complete final estimate before saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Parts and estimates may require repeated catalogue navigation, field copying and arithmetic.
tasks.enabler_now: Native catalogue links and fixed estimate formulas can remove duplicate entry and calculations.
tasks.still_hard: Compatibility, repair sequence and actual labour needs require technical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The technician recognises configuration differences and hidden work that a parts match misses.
tasks.altitude: Less estimate preparation; repair choices remain with the technician.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native service estimating functions can reuse selected parts and calculate quantity-times-price and labour costs; they do not choose safe repair procedures.

assumptions: Technician verifies actual identifiers and diagnosed need in s1, chooses parts and quantities in retained s2, and supplies actual initial labour hours and checks the rate/rule source there before calculation. Supplier catalogue supplies actual price and availability; missing or ambiguous matches remain manual.

S3 produces a provisional calculation only. S4 determines final procedures and labour requirements; any revised hours recalculate through the same native formula and are checked in s5. No free labour-time estimation or automatic compatibility decision is assumed.
Boundary ends with the internal estimate/plan. Any customer send, parts purchase or repair authorisation is its own actual final-version-gated action; no saving is claimed for those actions.
Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Native configuration first; already automated calculations earn no saving. Save remains one percent and uses the existing final check.
unknowns: Which catalogue fields are still copied manually?
research_questions: Can actual catalogue links reduce entry without increasing incompatible-parts errors?

incremental.description: Maintain parts field mappings and estimate rates/formulas.

approvals.approved_version: s5 checked final repair estimate and work plan and exact vehicle work-order destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 20*0.50 lookup + 20*0.50 parts entry + 10 calculation = 30; minus 1.5 upkeep = 28.5. Half eligible gives 15 minus 1.5 = 13.5. Compatibility, procedures, final check and save stay retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain proper vehicle-system operation to customers.

steps.what: Retrieve and check actual vehicle-system operating instructions for the customer's configuration
Explain proper operation of vehicle systems and demonstrate safe use to customers
Enter and check actual operating guidance in the existing service record
Save the checked final operating-guidance record

tasks.design: Configure native vehicle/manual links in {DOCS} and existing service-record references in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The technician checks the correct instructions, explains actual operation and records only guidance actually delivered.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer instruction may involve repeated manual lookup and service-reference entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native configuration-linked instructions and record defaults can reduce those steps.
tasks.still_hard: Safe demonstration and checking customer understanding require direct interaction.
tasks.human_edge: The technician adapts the explanation to actual controls and customer uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: Less lookup and reference entry; instruction remains personal.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: vehicle-linked manuals and native service-record defaults can reduce lookup and duplicate references; they do not replace safe demonstration.

assumptions: Actual manufacturer instructions and configuration identifiers already exist; technician verifies relevance in s1. Actual explanation and questions are captured in retained s3; no transcript or automatic evidence of understanding is assumed.
Only an existing guidance record is included. If absent, omit s3/s4 and reweight. Cuts are in repeated references, not conversation capture or safety instruction.
Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Already configured links earn zero saving; routine save retains one percent and uses the existing final check.
research_questions: Can existing configuration links reduce lookup while preserving demonstrations?

incremental.description: Maintain actual manual links and service-record defaults.

approvals.approved_version: s3 checked final actual operating-guidance record and exact vehicle destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 10*0.40 lookup + 9*0.20 reference entry = 5.8; minus 0.5 upkeep = 5.3. Half eligible gives 2.9 minus 0.5 = 2.4. Explanation, meaning capture and save stay retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Technicians keep examination, compatible-parts choices, repair planning and customer instruction while actual repeated preparation may shrink.
role.ambitious_version: Validate real duplicate work with native service functions before adding software.
